utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Ms. D'Ascoli, are you ready with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Next -- yes, next witness is Mr. Reshit Salihi and his evidence relates to paragraphs 72(a) and 77 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic -- it's Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to say something before the witness walked in. I just have this particular observation since we've had this 20-day break. It seems to me that the way in which these 92 bis witnesses are being heard - the witness can sit down, it doesn't matter - I think that they are getting a new meaning. I have received some documents today translated into Serbian, three pages, 20 or 30 paragraphs of changes with completely new evidence that hasn't been used until now at all. It seems to me that the spirit of Rule 92 bis is being - well, how should I put it? - evaded. Maybe we're moving on to 92 ter territory. That's the only thing I wish to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will look at that at a convenient time. Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat after me. I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: ... that I will speak the truth ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... that I will speak the truth ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: ... the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Ms. D'Ascoli has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness, could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Reshit Salihi.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And could you please state your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: 1947, I was born in Celine, in February.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: On which day in February?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, in February.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Do you remember the day?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I'm not educated.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Which is your current occupation, Mr. Salihi?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Farmer.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And where are you living at the moment?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: In Celine.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salihi, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in April 1999 and then an addendum in January 2002?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: In Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember if you provided a statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And have you recently had the opportunity to review this statement? Was this statement read back to you?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And during this review I remember that -- on the -- you indicated that the year of your birth indicated on the front page of this statement was not corrected because for the record this is the 65 ter number 02336. And the front page of this -- of the statement containing the witness's information reports that Mr. Salihi's date of birth is the 15th of February but 1940 rather than 1947.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That number is wrong. I was born in 1947 in February.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Perfect. Thank you. And, Mr. Salihi, other than that with this correction, are you satisfied that the information contained in your statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It is true and correct because I saw everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this statement, and it is the 65 ter number 02336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00632, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, do you remember you also testified about the same events in the Milutinovic et al. case in September 2006?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And have you recently had the opportunity to review your previous testimony? Was this testimony read back to you recently?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch what the witness said. Could the witness be asked to sit closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, could you please sit closer to the microphone. Thank you. And could you please repeat the answer to my question, and I had just asked you whether this -- your previous testimony in Milutinovic was recently read back to you. Could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We just had a problem with the interpretation. And, Mr. Salihi, does this transcript of your testimony accurately reflect your evidence, and would you testify to the same fact or in the same way today?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, everything is correct, and I will say the same things today that I said then.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this transcript into evidence, and it is the 65 ter number 05029.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00633, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thanks. And I will now read a summary of this witness's evidence. The witness describes the attack by Serb forces on the village of Celine in Orahovac municipality in March 1999. On the early morning of the 25th of March, 1999, Serb forces started shelling the village of Celine, looting and burning houses. Following this attack, part of the witness's family fled and left the house and family compound, while the witness remained there with some other family members. In the afternoon, as a group of policemen approached the witness's house, one of the witness's brothers was killed in front of the witness by a burst of automatic fire. The witness went hiding in the neighbourhood and later he fled to the forest where he remained there for three days until a group of policemen arrived to the forest. The policemen separated women and children from men, searched and robbed people, and then marched them back to the village at gun point. They were then forced to walk in a convoy in the direction of Prizren. The witness describes that after a march of about 30 minutes, a large number of trucks arrived. The police forced the villagers to board the trucks and transported them to Zhur, where they were ordered off the trucks and told to walk to Albania. The witness and his immediate family were then brought to a refugee camp in Tirana. And this is the end of the in-court summary. I will now proceed with some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, as you know, the Trial Chamber already has before it your previous testimony and statements, so I will just have a few questions for you. In your statement at page 2, paragraph 4, for the record, you referred to the shelling of your village, Celine, by Serb forces on the 25th of March, 1999, and you say that after the shelling Serb ground forces, I quote, "dressed in black uniforms entered the village." Can I just ask you who these Serb ground forces were or if you could define them better, please.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, they were Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you tell us what these forces did when they entered the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They entered the village. They started burning the village. They killed people and looted the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Also in your statement exactly you mentioned that the Serbs set fire to houses and buildings in the village, and I wanted to ask you whether this is something that you saw with your eyes, the fact that they were burning and looting houses?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And where were you located on the 25th of March, in the morning, when you observed all of this?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: At home. Because I could see the village, and I saw the infantry and the police when they entered, when they set the houses on fire, when they looted the houses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us to which ethnicity these houses were belonging, the houses that were looted and burned?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Albanians. Serbs never lived in our village, in Celina.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So there were no Serbs living in Celine I understand; right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salihi, in your statement - and for the record this is page 3, paragraph 3, and I think in the B/C/S version it's the beginning of page 4 - you described how, in the evening of the 25th of March, you fled to the nearby forest and then you remained there for three days. Can I ask you whether there were other people also gathered there?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The whole village was there, but there were also refugees from nearby villages that had fled their villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you know why those people were there, why they had to flee the other villages?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Because their houses were burning and the people of that -- those villages did not have anywhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you remember from which villages they had to flee?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. From Krusha e Madhe, Hoxha, Brestovc, Nagavci.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were hiding in the forest in those days, could you hear or see anything from there?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We could hear the shots from the village, the houses were burning, we could see the smoke billowing from the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, let's now move to the moment in which the policemen arrived, separated women and children from men, and then they brought you back to the village of Celine. Can I ask you what -- if you saw anything while passing through Celine while you were brought back to the village, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We couldn't see anything. We couldn't look up. We were isolated, we were surrounded, and we couldn't look around.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Were you escorted while you were brought back to the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Every 10 or 20 metres there was a different group of policemen, and they continued beating people up and ill treating them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So I understand you didn't have the chance of looking what was going on in the village, given the conditions in which you were ...

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't have a chance to see what was going on, but the village was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You remember seeing this fire around while you were walking or ...

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We could see the flames, the smoke, everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, you were then transferred by trucks to Zhur and then ordered by the police to walk to Albania. And can you tell us what happened at the border before entering Albania?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We were asked to hand over the IDs or any other documents. There were no problems there.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you do that, did you hand over your IDs at that moment at the border?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I handed over my document when I was in the Pisjak mountain, and at the border I did not have any ID or any money on me.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So at that moment you couldn't hand over your ID because you had done that already before in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I did not have it, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. Do you remember when you returned to Kosovo from Albania?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. Three months later.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you tell us what you found when you returned to your village in Celine three months later?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There was nothing in the -- left in the village. Whatever was there before was burnt, everything, the houses and everything in them had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And what about your house and your family compound?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: What did happen to your house and your family compound? Which were the conditions in which you found them when you returned to Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The houses were all burnt, as I said. When we went back we stayed in tents that we had received in Albania because we couldn't live in the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So also your house was burned and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It had been razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Salihi, was there a mosque in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And what about the mosque, how did you find the mosque when you returned to your village, in which condition was it?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The mosque had been razed to the ground as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you see this with your eyes of course?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes -- now -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'd like to call up the 65 ter number 02445, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell you -- may I?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you see the photograph on the screen, Mr. Salihi?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it. Can I show you? Can I point?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Oh, I would like to ask you whether you recognise what's depicted in this picture first of all.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Here you can see the wall, the surrounding wall, and the two trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: What's in the picture ? What can you see in the picture, first of all, besides the wall?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The mosque itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Which mosque is this, if you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The mosque in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And how can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: According to the picture, it looks like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You were mentioning the trees and the walls. Do these elements mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So I take it that this was the way in which the mosque in Celine looked like before its destruction?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this photograph into evidence, please. It's 65 ter number 02445.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00634, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, how many members of your family were killed in Celine on the 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And we're talking about your brother, Bajram; your brother Faik; his wife and five children; right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you know -- also know what happened to the Zeqiri family who joined you in your family compound on the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They were together with us, and they were there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you find out when you returned to Celine what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: When we went back, they were dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Were their bodies found anywhere?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you tell us where exactly if you know, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the yard where they were killed, and a group of people that had remained in the village had buried them; and when we went back we found them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you mean both the bodies of the Zeqiri families -- do you mean the bodies of the Zeqiri family?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, the Zeqiri family and my family because they were together.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So I understand their bodies were found together in the yard where supposedly they were killed?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: At the same place.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There was a foreign team there when we exhumed them. We gave them notes about the people who had been killed, then they were returned to us; and we reburied them in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Salihi, for having answered my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, do you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Salihi. I am Veljko Djurdjic, member of the Defence team for the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. Together with me is Ms. Marie O'Leary, member of the team. I will ask you to listen to me carefully so that we finish this examination as soon as possible. Since our conversation is being translated into several languages, I would kindly ask you to give me an answer once I've put my question. Bearing in mind the problems related to the year of your birth, it's been almost ten years since you gave your statement in Tirana, and it is only now that we establish that you were born seven years later. And to this day you don't know what the actual date of your birth was. However, do you know whether you were before -- born before or after the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: That I don't know. I was born in 1947. I really don't know when the Second World War or Third World War was. Maybe you do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but could you tell me whether you attended school at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me what is your mother tongue?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now start at the end of the examination-in-chief by my learned friend. You ended with your answer by saying that members of your family and the Zeqiri family were buried in the yard of your family property; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know who buried them?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you noted now that a team came and exhumed the bodies; am I right -- or to be more specific, not exhumed them but dug them out?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. Every parent gave the details of their family members, and then the foreigners took the bodies away to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the location where the exhumation was carried out photographed?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. The foreigners took photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think this is the third trial that you're testifying at. Were you able to see the photographs in the courtroom? Were you shown those photographs?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Even if they show me these photographs, I cannot say anything about them. I haven't finished any school, as you know. I cannot mark them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to look at Exhibit 634. It was admitted into evidence a little while ago. Mr. Salihi, is there a mosque without the minaret?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Ours had a minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, have you ever seen a mosque without the minaret?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't go around to see any other mosques. I had one in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, how was your mosque different from other mosques, apart from the fact that it was in your village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I can tell that this is our mosque from the entrance to the yard, from the surrounding wall, and from the two trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you agree with me that you cannot see the yard on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, you cannot see the yard for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on this photograph you're able to recognise the mosque by the wall, the wall that is here on the outside?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, based on that and the two trees that are shown on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salihi. Well, you can't actually see the mosque. You can only see the minaret and whatever is next to it.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You can see the building of the mosque too a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, just a little bit. Yes, I agree with you. You've told us that the people fled into the woods because their houses had been torched. Well, how could they all gather in the same place, people from different villages. You mentioned Nagavci, Krusa, Brestovac, if I'm not mistaken, your village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, people were fleeing their homes. They were going to family's in-laws with their families. So when the houses were set on fire, everybody with their families left for the mountain of Pisjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you. How come that you were all in the same place, yet Orahovac was nearby as far as I know and Prizren was close by, Pirane, Zrze? So how come that you all headed into the mountains towards Mount Pisjak?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It was impossible for the people to move around. They were all looking for shelter. We were surrounded from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how do you know about the other villages, Brestovac; Krusa, Velika, Mala; and Nagavci?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Not Krusha e Vogel but Krusha e Madhe. As I said earlier, people had families in villages and that's where they took shelter. They had nowhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said Mount Pisjak. I went through all the geographical maps and I never found this name, this mountain. Could you please tell me how far is this Mount Pisjak from your village, the place where you sought shelter in the woods that you called Pisjak?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's about 2 kilometres away. I didn't measure the distance, but this should be the approximate distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will go back to some photographs later, and we will perhaps be able to determine that with some precision. Mr. Salihi, you told us you were a farmer. Was your father a farmer too?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your father alive in 1999 when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No. He died 25 years earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I am right, you had six brothers?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were all brothers alive in 1999 when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were your other brothers farmers too?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell me, after your grandfather died, was the property divided?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, we have all the property together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you understand me correctly. I wasn't asking you about the father's property, but your inheritance from your grandfather. So was there a division of property or did you all live together in a commune of sorts?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We own everything together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So can I then conclude that with your uncles and their children and your family, that you all lived in a commune?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Everybody has his house, but we live all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was the head, the elder, of the commune?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You mean from my brothers?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, or uncles, whatever.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: My brother Bajram was the eldest.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many houses were there in your family property?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Six brothers, six houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the surface area of that place where the houses were?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: About 20 acres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now around this family compound where the houses were, was there a wall dividing the compound from the rest of the place?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Miftar Zeqiri who was my neighbour and still is, he had his own wall too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And was there a gate whereby one entered into your family compound?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Everyone can enter his house from the main road through an entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How tall was the wall?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, I didn't measure it, but it's less than 2 metres I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the gate made of?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. You mean the door built within the wall or ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the ones that were built into the wall and that opened to allow entrance into your family property.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Wooden gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the wall made of?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Bricks, red bricks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any agricultural machinery?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We had horses. We used them to work on the land.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you perhaps have a truck or some passenger cars?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salihi, as regards the division of labour, your contribution to this commune was only to work the land, or did you go to other places to sell the produce?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, on the market and everywhere where we could win or earn our bread. We didn't choose the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I then conclude that you left Celine to go to other places; and if yes, can you tell me what places you went to?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Prizren, Gjakove, and Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How much land did you own?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: 2 hectares.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have on our screens the Defence document D002-5633.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, can you tell us this road that we can see on the right-hand side of this photograph, do you know where this road leads to?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: As I said in the earlier -- as I said earlier, I cannot help you with this because I haven't finished any school. I cannot mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, I didn't ask you to mark anything. I just asked you to tell me. You can see as well as anyone else, so I'm just asking you whether you know this. And you live there, you say that you travelled to Djakovica and to Prizren, so this is the photograph of Celine and the area around it. So -- okay, I'm not going to ask you about the road, but could you tell me, you see the village of Celine, can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Please, I cannot distinguish between the roads because I cannot read the map. I cannot tell anything on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well I'm not going to ask you anything about the roads, but could you show where your house in Celine was?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I cannot help you at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well, but can you help me, can you tell me where your house was in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I really don't understand your question. I'm here to tell you about what I went through, what I experienced. This is the main purpose I'm here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Salihi, that's precisely why I'm asking you these questions. I want you to tell me where your house in Celine was because as far as I can recall from your statements you talk about that house, not only your house but other buildings, houses that belonged to other people, and I'm going to be asking you questions about those too.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours. I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I think that the witness has already answered and has indicated that he cannot help with this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Counsel is entitled to explore whether he has any visual recognition of the picture depicted by the map. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I accepted the fact that the witness is unable to visually recognise things here, so we have to take the long road here. I'm asking him on the basis of his life in the village where the house was, and then I will have to determine where other buildings were and whether he could -- well, I want to check, verify, his statement. Maybe he doesn't want to answer my questions, then let him say so; and I will not insist on the answer. But then it's a whole different situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, do you understand me? Forget about the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please remove the map from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you where your family property was in the village of Celine.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know what is going on. As I said, I cannot read the map, I cannot pin-point my house on the map because that would be a lie, and I'm not here to lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sure that you have come here to tell the truth, so could you please tell me where your house, your family property, in Celine was?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I can describe it using words. It was on the lower part, the part that connects Krusha e Madhe and Celine. And there is a river separating us. This is what I can say as far as the location of my house is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far from your house was the railroad?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I mentioned the river, right, the Krusha river? Is this what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you about the railway tracks, how far were they from your house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Now I understand it, the railway tracks, about 1.000 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me the Prizren-Djakovica road, how far was it from your house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The road is close to the railway tracks, the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please tell me, your house, where was it in relation to the Nagavci road?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It's very close to us. We -- our fields are close to each other. It's not very far.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were referring to the land that you farmed, and I was talking about your house and the Nagavci road, so just to get some bearings here. So how far is that road from your house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You have to go through Krusha e Madhe, then to Nagavc, and then Hoxha, Brestovc, Rahovec, that's the direction of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is your house on the Nogavac road?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, no, we live in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I understand that, but I'm asking you whether your house was on the road leading to Nogavac, and if not if you could explain to us where the road leading to Nogavac was.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You have to go to the main road of Celine, go through Krusha e Vogel, and then turn to Nagavc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's clear this up. The black-top road from Prizren to Djakovica has an off-shoot that leads to Celine; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This road that veers from the main road to go to Celine, it's not a black-top road, it's a dirt road; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it used to be, but now it is asphalted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But now tell me, the road from Celine to Bela Crkva, was there some kind of a local road?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, because the Celine road is linked to Bellacerke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But -- now, where was your house in relation to that road?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The road to Bellacerke, not to Krusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, not towards Bellacerke -- if you go to the main road, yes, but not otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My previous question - and this is why I followed up on it - is: Was there a local road linking Celine with Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, my follow-up question was: Where was your house in relation to this local road going from Celine to Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It's far away from that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if you agree with me, Bela Crkva is to the west of Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Bellacerke is next to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well, but the main road from Prizren to Djakovica - and given the location of the village of Celine - is your house in the part of the village that is closer to the main road, that would be the southern part of the village, is this where your house is?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, it's not close to the main road. We're in the upper part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me where is the school in relation to your family compound?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The school is further up. It's above the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is the mosque in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, it is beyond the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you take the road, how far is from your house to the school building?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It's quite a bit of a walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I right if I say that it takes even longer to walk to the mosque from your house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you tell me if you know whether there is a village leader in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't think there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever attend any meeting that was attended by all the heads of all the families in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There were no meetings of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know a person by the name of Agim Jemini?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see him in The Hague now?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where his house was in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He does not live close to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us where he lives?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You mean Agim?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: He lives in the same village in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what you told us, but where is his house in relation to your house? Could you explain that.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I did say that he lives far from my house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you explain to us what you mean when you say that it is far away from your house? Could you be more specific.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I did not measure the distance. He lives on the road that links my place to the main road, and that's where he lives. I have to go on that road in order to get to the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is when you go in one direction, and if you go in the opposite direction from his house, where does that road lead to?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There is only one road. It doesn't go anywhere else. This road passes by Agim's house and there is no other road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, it leads to the main Prizren-Djakovica road?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in the opposite direction, so if you're not going towards Agim's house, so if you go to the left or uphill, wherever this road leads to, where does it end?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It links with Krusha, so that's where it ends, in Krusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salihi, in paragraph 2 of your statement you say: "Up until March this year, my family and myself were able to live relatively normally in light of the overall situation in Kosovo." Could you tell us what the situation was, and what do you mean when you say that you were able to live relatively normally?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, up until the time when what I described happened, we lived normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I conclude that up until the war you lived a normal life?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, normal life. We did have problems, a lot of problems earlier, but not the kind of problems we had then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in the same paragraph you say: "In actual fact, because there were no Serbs in the area where our village is, the problems that occurred in Kosovo for the most part did not affect our lives." Could you explain this to me. What does that mean, what you said?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain. There were no Serbs living in Celine at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. So why were there no problems then, or rather, why are there problems when there are Serbs there, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I did not say that. The problems happened on the 25th, after they came.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would like us to move on faster, but again I have to read part of your statement to you. In paragraph 2 you said: "In fact, as there were no Serbs living in our village area, our lives were more or less untouched by the troubles going on in Kosovo." Could you explain that to me? Does that mean there are problems if there are Serbs there; and if there are no Serbs there, there are no problems?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No. Even those places where Serbs lived, they did not have any problems really, before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So can we conclude then that this part of your statement was misinterpreted?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It has not been understood correctly --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why has it not been understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You told me that there were no problems with the Serbs, without the Serbs, and that this was wrongly written up in your statement, what I read out to you, that that's not what you said, that those who compiled the statement - because you did not compile it - compiled it the wrong way?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, they did not make a mistake. In Celine there were no Serbs living there, and we did not have any problems. And each village, whether they had problems or not, they know about their own problems. I don't know about everything that happened in Kosova. I did not say anything about the rest of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said because there are no Serbs that the problems that were occurring in Kosovo for the most part did not affect your life. That is what you said. Now I'm asking you: What were the problems that existed in places where there were Serbs, those that affected lives in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know why you're delving into these things. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just reading your own statement out. I'm not doing anything else. Since you cannot explain this to me, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I cannot respond here about events in other villages. I am here to describe the events in my village. I am here to testify about them. I cannot testify about things that happened in other villages in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you mentioned problems to those who you talked, that you mentioned problems that happened in Kosovo and that did not affect you and your life because there were no Serbs there. Is that what you said or is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: What I said is there were no Serbs in my village and there were no problems. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you find out that the war had started?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, the war started on the 25th of March - I will never forget that - when we woke up in the morning we were surrounded on all sides. Police and army forces had surrounded Celine, and then everything that I described earlier happened. They started burning, massacring. The police did all that, not the army. I want to emphasize that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go ahead and say whatever else you have to say, but I would kindly ask you to answer my questions so that we would keep this cross-examination as short as possible. So my question was: How was it that you found out that the war had started, if you had found out at all that is?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know about generally. I know about the things you asked me about in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, you still remember some dates from that period to this day; am I not right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: What dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: March 1999, for example.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, that one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you right now what was it that made you remember some particular dates, how come you remembered them?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I remember those dates because we suffered all the evils possible, the whole Kosovan population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said to me a few moments ago that you woke up in the morning. What time was it when you got up?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, I did not look at my watch; however, I have to say here, as I said the other times I was here, I did not look at my watch, I don't know what the exact time was. It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time did you wear a wrist-watch?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I did not keep a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to ask you about the time because that is interesting. There are many exact hours that are referred to in your statement, 8.00, 9.00, 10.00 in the evening, so that's why I'm asking you. Please don't hold it against me. Now that you've said this, I'm not going to ask you about any particular point in time. So what you had said was that it was the morning. So may I conclude that it had dawned?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I said whether it was 5.00 or 6.00 or 7.00 in the morning I don't know, I did not look at the clock or watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You didn't look at your watch or clock, but was it daylight when you got up?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, it was daylight when we woke up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where is your room in the house that you live in?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: How can I describe it to you? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right, let's try to deal with this some other way. I'll put questions and you give me answers. Does -- do you live in a one-storey house, is there just a ground floor?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: My house is G-shaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there are several houses there, is your house the one that's the closest to the road or what is its position in relation to the other houses?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Close to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you leave the house when you woke up, on the 25th of March as you said?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I told my children to leave, and I stayed at home myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please let's do this slowly. You said that you had woken up, that it was day-time. I'm asking you whether you left your house or whether you just stayed there in your house.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I was in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As you say in your statement, you saw the army surrounding the area of the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. I went to my brother's house, the one that was killed. His father is a little bit further up. And from the yard I could see the army. Above the mosque they also had tanks. I also described this in my statement. And they started shelling and shooting. They did not cause any damage to the population, but later the police came in groups, they burned the houses, they killed people, and they looted. The army did not cause any damage to the village; the police forces did, and this is why I'm here, to testify, to describe the things that really happened and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salihi. Please give me short answers and only to the questions that I'm putting to you. What you talked about just now was very extensive, but I didn't really ask you about anything about any of this. Let me just ask you another thing before the technical break. Why did you go up there to your brother's house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I went to my brother's house to see what was going on in the village. That's why I went there. I just went to another house in my village. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how was it that you knew that something was going on in the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: But we were surrounded. There was shelling, and we could hear shots, so we knew that something was going on. We saw them with our own eyes. I'm not lying here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think it is time for the technical break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic. We must have a break now, and we will resume in half an hour, at 1.00. There is a consternation that this may be the equivalent of the lunch break. We will resume at 1.15. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, you told us a little while ago that you left your home in the morning and that you went to your brother's house. Could you tell me, what were you wearing when you left the house?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Normal clothes, as I am wearing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After you left the house in the morning and until you left your family property, did you go back to your house at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We were staying together. Our houses are one after the other, next to each other. My brothers have a house just like I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you intend to do? What would you have done had the events that unfolded not unfolded?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I would have gone and worked on the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, I was not wearing a suit probably, but normal clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw there, further up from the village by the mosque, when you saw those forces, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Nothing. We just observed what they were doing. What else could we do?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to what you explained to us that you saw, did you see the forces anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The whole village was surrounded by Serb forces, army and police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We could see that. We experienced that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what is it that you went through?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, we were just staying there when they started shelling, killing people, burning houses, until the moment when they came up to -- very close to my house when they killed eight people. I saw everything. I saw the fire and the killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us this several times and then you repeat it yet again. My question was: How did you know that the village was surrounded on all sides?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You could see that. The people could see that. We knew, all of us, that we were surrounded; it was obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I don't know what the others saw, but tell me what did you see? You say that you only saw something there above the mosque.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I saw them and I told you about the tanks over the part where the mosque was. There were army forces there and police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this the only thing that you saw?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No. Everybody could see that we were surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salihi, do you know what the word "method" means?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I don't know what "method" is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me what does Serb land forces mean? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I can say that the land forces came in and they caused damage to the population. They were infantry. They came on foot. They did all those evil things to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what your military specialty was?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I was infantry. I was issued a weapon. I had a rifle. I didn't have any education, but I did know the military rules in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, just tell me one more thing, do you mean "infantry" when you say "ground forces"?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, but for the police infantry, not the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said to us today, I think it was on page 7 of the transcript, line 6, that you saw the infantry and the police entering the village. So I would be interested in what the difference is between the police and the infantry?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, the army entered the village. They saw that the civilians had nowhere to go. They were running in panic. Children were crying. So they don't harm anyone in the village. Then the infantry of the police forces entered the village. They went to houses, set them on fire, looted the houses, killed people. They did the most evil things to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that the army shelled the village on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They did shell, but they didn't cause any harm to the civilian population. They were aware that the civilians had nowhere to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where were you when the army shelled the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: In my house, in the courtyard. As all the others, I was observing what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I understood things, your yard is on flat land?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, but it's a little bit on an elevation. There are trees there, but we could observe the movements in the village from there very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were these shells falling, tell me?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: On the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the place where you were in the yard, how far away could you see?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know how far away I could see, but the most important thing is that I could see everything that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But your village is big. You cannot see all of it. It's bigger than that. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: But I was on such a vantage point that I could see everything, where people were going to. It is a big village, as you said, it has about 200 houses, but I could see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that there was shooting in the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: From where? Or by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That there was shooting in the village. That's what I'm asking you about. You said there was shooting in the village, so was there? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, the police was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the outskirts of the village you saw that it was only the police who were shooting; right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, as I said in the beginning, it was the army that entered the village. They saw that the population was leaving in panic, and then the infantry and the police came in the village, inside the village. They looted the houses, they set the houses on fire, and killed those that they found in the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, from the place where you were standing to the outskirts of the village, what is the distance as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know the distance. I didn't measure it, but I could see very well from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you could see houses that were on the outskirts of the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did these houses have walls around their yards?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, some had, some didn't. But even if all of them had walls you could see very well which houses they entered and which houses they set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could one see whether there was shooting coming from that -- from those houses?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, how do you know that it was the police who were wearing black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We call it blue. And they had those kind of colour on their uniforms, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, in all your statements so far you've said the uniforms were black. How come you're now saying black is something you call blue?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They worked in groups, different groups changed. They killed so many people. I could have been one of those killed too. They were different groups of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of your statement it says: "The Serb forces that had entered the village were wearing black uniforms, although I was too far away from them to see the insignia on their uniforms."

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They looked black from that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Not to spend too much time on this, in the Milutinovic trial you said that you saw such black uniforms before the war too.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Before the war it's impossible for me to have seen them before the war. I did see them on that day; and, as I said, every 20 metres there was a different group and all these different groups took turns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have to get back to this later then. Not to waste time now, could you please tell me where was it that you saw these policemen? From what direction were they coming? At what location were they?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I will repeat it again. The village was surrounded by them. They know best from what direction they were coming and where they were. The whole village was surrounded by policemen. They could enter the village from any side they wished.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, I do apologise but you have been testifying about them entering the village. I'm just asking you where they had come from, from what direction. I'm just asking you to tell me what you had seen, not what others knew. I'm asking you about what your own immediate observations were. If you saw them, then tell me what was it that you saw. You're not talking about the police only. You are talking about combat armoured vehicles and tanks and so on and so forth. So when was it that you first saw these policemen?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: When they [as interpreted] woke up, we saw that the village was surrounded by policemen and by the army. Then they entered the village from every side, from all the sides. They could do whatever they wanted. When we woke up, we were surrounded, as I already explained. The army did shoot, but they did not cause any harm to the population because they could see that the population was running in panic. And then the police entered and they looted the house and committed all sorts of crimes. This is what I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Again you are not answering my question. You are speaking in general terms about the police surrounding the village and that other things happened afterwards. What does this word mean in your vocabulary, "surrounded"?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Surrounded by the police and the army. This is what I said, and I'm repeating again that the army did not cause any harm or damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us leave the army aside. As for what you've said to us until now, you said that you just saw something above the mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What colour were the tanks that you saw?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The tanks were of the army. They were on tracks. They had the colour of the grass, as we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I didn't see the armoured vehicles, where they left them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that you were not an eye-witness to the burning of the mosque and school?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes as far as the school is concerned, and no as far as the mosque is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far away were you from the school?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I was far, but you could see very well, they entered the school, they set it on fire, and then they went to the houses and did whatever they wanted to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how the school was torched, did you see that?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know what they used to torch the school, but I did see the flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There was constant noise. They were using their weapons, they entered the houses freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you establish how many houses were burned?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They torched many, many houses. When we returned from Albania, we realised that the whole village was turned into ashes. All of it was burned and looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, where were you when you noticed that people were leaving the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I already told you. I was in the courtyard of my brother. We were sitting there, and we could see that the people were fleeing from their houses and looking for shelter for their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me from what houses these people were fleeing, from which parts of the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The whole village, everybody was trying to leave. Everybody was looking for shelter for his own family. They were trying to withdraw them from the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what did they do? Where did they go?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They left the village and then they gathered, as I already mentioned, in the Mount of Pisjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see Mount Pisjak from your yard?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As you stood in your yard, how could you know that they were fleeing towards that mountain?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: At around 3.30 in the afternoon, after they killed eight members of my family and 14 members of the Zeqiri family, when it became dark I went to Pisjak to find my family. I found them at around 10.00 p.m., and my family and I joined the rest of the people who were gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You came to this place where your family was, and it was only then when you established where they were. You did not know when you stood in your yard where they were; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I could only see that they were leaving the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Previously was there some kind of an agreement reached, say with the neighbours and everybody else, where you were supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Nobody knew in advance where they were going to. They left because they had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, in the Milutinovic case on page 4219, that's the transcript page, in response to the question put by His Honour Judge Bonomy, you said that before the war you saw policemen. And then you were asked whether you could remember what kind of uniform they wore, and you said that ten of them had black uniforms. That's what we discussed a few moments ago. You said at line 10 that they had black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, but they changed. They were wearing all sorts of uniforms. They wore whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't understand what this means, that they were changing their clothes all the time.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: As I said, they could do whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 5 you said that the members of your family left the farm that morning at about 5.30 to hide in the nearby forests. We've explained the bit about the forests. Tell me, why didn't you go with them?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I didn't go because I asked my brothers to leave all together, but they said no. So I decided to stay there. It was my own house I was staying in after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you were left there and your brother Bajram and Faik, and you say that with Faik there was also his four-member or five-member family.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you all leave?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I will tell you now. Had we known that what happened would happen, we would have left too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you stay to defend your farm?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, I thought that they would do no harm; however, they did us harm. They did these evil things to us, and here we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you stay on to defend your farm?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: If I could, I would have defended my family members, not the house, not my property.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to that too. But could you explain this to me now, you said that Miftar Zeqiri was your next-door neighbour. Why did he come to you, to your farm, with his 14 family members?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The yards are adjacent to each other. For us it was like one same house, you know, the whole family gathered there, and we stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What time was it when Zeqiri came to you together with his family?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It was in the morning when the children woke up. I didn't look at a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But most of your family had already left your family farm, and you also say that everybody else from the village had left for the most part. But then you said that Zeqiri came to you.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We live next door. He is my first-door neighbour, and we spent time together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the moment they came to your yard, where were you actually, you and Zeqiri and the members of your family?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: As I already said, they were together there. My eldest brother stood up, Bajram stood up. They -- there was a house there which was not yet finished, and the police shot at him and killed him. When he was killed, I left. The infantry came later on, and they massacred everybody, the children, everybody who was there. A 6-month-old baby was massacred there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you're not answering my question. Please listen to me carefully. This is my question: When the Zeqiri family came, where were you, and where were they? That was my question. Just tell me where were you. And we are going to get to this thing that you've been telling me all along.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I did say where I was. I was there. I can't remember how many times I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, you have six houses, a big yard. You also told us what the area of your family farm was. I am asking you: Where were you, you and the other 14 members of your family and Zeqiri, where were you? At 3.00 in the afternoon, I'm not asking you that, you didn't have a watch or a clock, so I'm not asking you that, but where were you?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I told you that I was together with them. I don't know what else to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you can tell me, I was in a house. And then I ask you, Which house? Or you can tell me, I was standing at this particular place in the yard. But you did not mention the house at all from the morning hours until now. So that's why I'm asking you: Where were you actually?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I was in my brother's yard. We were all there. The Zeqiri family was there as well. I don't know how else to describe it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So may I conclude that you were outside the house from the morning onwards, you were in the yard?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Where was it that you first saw the Serb police when they reached your yard?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We were there when we saw them, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where were the police when you first saw them?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They came and entered the village from the school, and they came down towards where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: We could see them coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did they walk along the street?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There was no road, but you could see them entering the houses and coming out of the houses everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
