utterances.text: I'm asking you quite specifically about your family compound. When was it that they got in? Please listen to me carefully.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You mean my family?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean the moment when you started talking about the police coming into your family compound, where did you see the police for the first time? Where were they? Did you see them at all before they entered?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I saw them before they entered the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And after that, when did you see them for the first time?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I told you the direction they were coming from. I could see them entering houses, coming out of the houses. This is the hundredth time I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you keep repeating the same thing, and you're not answering my question and that's our problem. As far as I was able to understand, in front of your family compound there is only one road, and it leads to Agim Jemini's house and towards Velika Krusa going in the opposite direction. And the school is further up from you, several kilometres, I don't know what you said. And now I'm talking about the police in front of your house, where did you see them, how did you see them, and you keep telling us that you saw them at the school. But let us go back. What is an assault rifle to your mind?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: May I speak, please? May I respond to this gentleman? I don't think he's understanding me. Or maybe he doesn't want to understand me. Can I speak, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The police did not climb the road as you are saying, but they went from house to house and they set them on fire. They killed people in their own houses. They did not kill people on the street. And they did not go towards Agim's house or whoever you're mentioning. I did not see them go there. They went from house to house, and they did whatever they wanted there. And this is what I described to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that's what you described to us, but now we're coming to the point in time when they reached your house. And I don't have any bad intentions here; I just want you to explain some things to us. When did you see them for the first time? When they reached your house, where were they?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I told you earlier, but I'll try to explain. There was a house close to Zeqiris' house which had not been finished yet, the construction. The police was there. We did not see them. And it's from there that they shot my brother who stood up. The bullet caught him, and he was killed instantly. And then I left the house. There was a group of five that I saw with my own eyes. The infantry came to where my family was and the Zeqiri family was, and they massacred them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, what do you mean when you say an assault rifle?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know because I was not together with them to see what kinds of weapons they were carrying. We were trying to go and hide. They knew what kinds of weapons they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you this because in paragraph 5 in the penultimate sentence there is mention of assault rifles, and I wanted you to explain what it means. So could you please tell me, the police officers that entered your farm, what kind of uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They were in different groups. They were wearing blue uniforms. They had red and some of them white ribbons. I don't know what else to tell you because I was not staying with them to be able to describe them in detail. I'm only telling you what I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 6 you say: "Suddenly three bursts of automatic gun-fire were fired at our farm. I saw Bajram hit in the abdominal area and killed instantly." Could you please tell me where your brother Bajram was at this time that you describe in paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. There were only 5 metres between us. I was there, in the yard, where he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And where was he?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I told you, he was there near me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that he was in the yard?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: In the yard, in Faik's yard, the family was there, Zeqiri's family was there. We were all together there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, did you see the person or persons that actually opened fire?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: After Bajram was killed, I told you that I left and I could see them coming down. The infantry then went in. I can't imagine how they could do those things to the people, even the little children. How could they do all those things to the Kosovar people? The whole world was distressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, my question is this: At the time when you were in the yard, did you see where the gun-fire came from and did you see who opened fire? And now you're telling me what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, I did tell you that they came out of that house. As I said Miftar Zeqiri had this house, that the construction of which had not finished yet. They left the house where they shot from and came to the yard where my brother was there with his children and the Zeqiri family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how far is it from the gate of your family farm, to the Zeqiri -- to the gate on the Zeqiri farm?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There is a fence that divides us and we're next-door neighbours. There's only a fence between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and this is why I'm asking you, because there was this fence, how far was it from the gate on your family farm to the gate on the Zeqiri farm?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: My brother's house, where we had gone to at that time, is next to Miftar Zeqiri's house, so they're next-door neighbours and that's why they came all together to stay where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But again you didn't tell me how far is it from the gate to your family farm to the gate of the Zeqiri farm.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They're not very far from each other. There is just a fence between us, as I said; and because they're not very far, they came and joined us in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But it was much earlier than the events when there was this gun-fire when your brother was hit; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: 3.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And did I understand it right that at that time the Zeqiris were in your yard?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: But the yards are next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, a little while ago you told us that the Zeqiris had come to seek shelter at your place and that they were in your yard. Were they in your yard when your brother was hit?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I told you that they're next to each other. Ours is here, theirs is there, and there is where they were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There is a misunderstanding it seems. This is a question, a yes or no question. Were the Zeqiris in your yard at the time when your brother was hit?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Between the two, there is a fence and they were on both sides. On that border they were all together, they had gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that some members of the Zeqiri family were with you in the yard?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I did not say that. Both families were there. The children were there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where is "there"? Could you please tell me that.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: In my brother's yard which borders Zeqiris' house and yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So they were in your yard. Now I want to know how far were your brother and your other family members from you and your brother Bajram when he was hit?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They were all in one group there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far away from them were you?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I told you, about 5 metres away from him, maybe not even that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And why did you flee to Miftar Zeqiri's farm after the shooting, as you say?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I did not say that. If I had gone to Zeqiri's house, I would have died as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I will have to read from paragraph 6 of your statement. "I saw Bajram hit in the abdominal area and killed instantly. Faik and his family remained with the Zeqiri family in our compound, while I ran next door into the Zeqiri compound."

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then it goes on to say: "Where I found the 3-foot hole to hide in (about 90 centimetres)" --

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I did not measure it, but it was of that kind of depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well, but where is this hole where you hid?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It was above the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Whose?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Our houses, all of them, and our neighbour's house, Miftar Zeqiri's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you were outside of the family compound, both your family compounds, yours and Zeqiri's, you were in that group?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think I told you that when my brother was killed, I left, I fled. Because they were coming towards us, so I left the place I was together with them. And then they entered, and they did what I already told you several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where did you flee? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I stayed in that hole until it became dark, and I left then when it became dark to go to find my family in the mountain. I found them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, you are a farmer, yet you went to big towns to sell your produce there, so you understand me very well. You know what I mean when I'm asking you this. My question is: Where is the hole where you hid? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Where I hid?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where is the hole where you hid when your brother was shot?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I told you that I fled. There is the side of the mountain there, of the hill, beyond our houses, the whole neighbourhood, and that is where I hid, in a hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But could you please explain to us, we don't know that, where are the slopes beyond your houses where you went?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know, why you are asking me in such detail where we hid and so on. People were killed, and you're not asking about them. You're asking where we hid and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No. Had I had a weapon, I might have been able to save someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did the Zeqiris have weapons?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know. I can only tell you things about myself. I know things about myself and what I did. That's why I'm here, to respond to you about those things.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how many times I have to tell you. Had we had a gun, we wouldn't have stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question - it appears that I need to repeat it - was whether Faik had any weapons?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know that he had any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me, do you speak Serbian and did you speak Serbian at the time?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I can understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 6 you say that you heard someone shout: "Shoot, there are terrorists here." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, this I heard very well. Everybody was terrorist to them, children, the whole of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And where were there terrorists?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. And who are terrorists to your mind?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... we heard this term. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that at one point in the evening you came to the place where your family was, and in paragraph 7 you say that the next day a group of 40 policemen arrived in the forest. Did you see the police officers?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 28th of March, when we had to leave the mountain?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean the first morning after you escaped from the hole and went into the woods, so that's the next morning. According to your calculation, it should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I must interrupt you. What the witness says that he remained there for the next three days, and then the next morning after that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. That's correct. I do apologise. You are correct. That's the morning that I mean. So two -- after two or three days spent in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So that morning when the policemen came, that's the morning that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: You see that we can easily make mistakes here. Which date are you referring to now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The 28th of March is the correct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, when they made us leave. There were so many groups, almost more policemen than civilians. Whether they were 40 or more, that I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 -- well, I don't want to make a mistake again - you say 40 policemen arrived. And I wanted to ask you, where did they come from, from what direction, if you saw them actually arrive?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They were shooting from the top of the mountain, and we saw them when we were there in the meadow. We couldn't see the direction they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you in a meadow or in a forest?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I was in the forest, but in the morning when they made us leave, we gathered on a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that there were 40 policemen there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The reference is over 40 policemen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't count them because we saw thousands of them later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me -- I'm asking you this because your statement contains figures. It would never have crossed my mind to put this kind of question to you otherwise. You mentioned 10.000 people here. Is that your own estimate? Is it somebody else's estimate? How come this is here?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: There were many civilians because the whole of the population stopped there. The population of my village was there. There were a lot of people. Maybe there was not exactly this figure of 10.000, maybe there were 8.000, maybe there were more, but there were a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. I would actually like to go back. When we said that you had heard that someone said that there were terrorists there, did you say that there was shooting that went on for 15 minutes? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know now to what event or location you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean I went back to the period when those policemen had come and when somebody had said: "Shoot, there are terrorists here." Then you say the shooting went on for 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: This is when they killed the members of my family, my brother's family. Then I heard when these infantry forces came in they were shouting between them. They entered the yard, and they killed them on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you actually see that?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, I only heard that, and I saw them leaving, going downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether you know what the UCK is, as in KLA?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, this was of no interest to me. I didn't bother who was what. My statement is about what these forces committed over the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Correct. But I asked you whether you could tell me what the UCK is.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I cannot really answer that because I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please don't understand this as a provocation on my part. I am asking you this because in your statement in paragraph 12 it says: "Since I have lived all my life in Celine, I can say that in my village there were never any members of the OVK," it says in Serbian and it is UCK in Albanian. So I'm asking you: Do you know what the UCK is?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I did say that there was no UCK in Celine. As to what this means and what is the meaning of it, that I don't know, and that was never of any interest to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Before giving your statement, did you ever hear of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear of the KLA, but I was not interested in finding out what it meant, who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us accept that. How is it that you know then that there were no members of the KLA in the village then?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I know that because I didn't see anyone leaving the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if someone was in the village, he didn't have to leave and didn't have to be a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 7 of your statement you say that the police searched you when you were up there in the forest, when they arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: That is correct. When we left the forest, when they made us leave, they separated the men [as interpreted] and the children from the men. They made us, the men, into three groups. They asked for our personal identification documents. They collected everything and then they collected the money. They didn't want the Serbian dinars. They wanted Deutschemarks, so whatever we had on us, we took it out, and they collected. And they killed a very young man, Agim Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was whether the police had searched you. Am I right actually?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the police find something when searching you?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in your statement you say that they searched you and that they ordered you to hand over 5.000 Deutschemarks.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] correct. [Albanian interpretation]Absolutely correct. We just threw them in front of us. They threatened to kill us. They had knives on them, daggers. So everybody from the civilians threw on the ground whatever they had on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was after the search. Now tell me, you got dressed in the morning in order to go out and work on the field and then you say that you were in your yard and along with you you had 5.000 Deutschemarks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Listen, I want us to understand each other. We woke up in the morning. We had to run for our lives. There were no conditions for us to go and work on the land as we usually did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that it is time for the technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Djurdjic. I thought you said you had only one more question. I misunderstood, did I?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall be very brief. It's not that I have too much left, but then there was that question that I had forgotten and then I had to go back to that. It's going to be very brief. I'm getting close to the end, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have then the second break now and resume at a quarter past 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I apologise that I was delayed by a few moments by another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, am I right when I say that you were not an eye-witness when your daughter handed over 6.000 German marks and when the police took her gold necklace?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They were stopped at Krusha e Vogel. They were beaten up there, and my daughter told me that they had taken away her money and the necklace.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are -- so I am right that you were not an eye-witness?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't. My daughter described it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, do you know Agim Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Agim Ramadani was?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: He was a young man about 17 or 18 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: From Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did he live in Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: He lived in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where that house is?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you personally know Agim Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you friends with his family?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No, no. He is just a co-villager.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: His father is a farmer as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me what he wore, what Agim Ramadani wore when the police came up there to the forest?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Normal clothes as anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see him before the police came?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, when we left the mountain, I saw him. We were gathered together. We were made to stand on rows, and he was close to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far away were you from him?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: About 20 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did I understand correctly that the police singled him out and took him somewhere?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, they singled him out. About 30 metres away they beat him up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see them searching him?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was something found on him when he was searched?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: They did not find anything on anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say the police separated you into two groups, not to go into the number of people involved, and you say that many trucks came to transport you then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes, we were kept near the road all day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was any family member with you?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, my son who was 13 years old was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the rest of your family was in another group; right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, all the women were separated from us. We didn't know where they were sent to, but later on we heard that they had been at Krusha e Vogel. That was the rest of my family with the women.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Arben your son's name?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know what year he was born?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Now he is 20 or 21 years old, maybe 22. I can't tell you exactly, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you this because your statement seems to show that the women and children were separated from the men?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, when we were made to climb down the mountain, we were separated. We didn't know where they sent the women and the children. We learned that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yet in the statement it says that Arben was 15 at the time.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Maybe I did, but still I'm not sure, 14 maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that in -- you saw in a newspaper article in Albania that members of Faik's family and of the Zeqiri family had been killed?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No. I knew about that when they were killed on the spot; however, the newspapers wrote about the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of the statement you gave, you mention that you were afraid that something horrible had happened to them, yet you say that you saw the article in the newspaper -- well, it's different from what you're saying now.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I can't read the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I know that, but this is what it says in your statement, not that you read but that you saw -- but okay, let's move on. Do you know the name Ekrem Rexha?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the Hoca river-bed is?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Hoqe e Vogel?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was your family there when it left the village?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: My family went to Pisjak. I didn't say that they went to the Hoqe river.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm asking you whether they went to the Hoca river-bed.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying. Which Hoqe? There is no such thing as Hoqe. My children were sent to Krusha e Vogel, then loaded on trucks, and sent over to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about that, Mr. Salihi. I'm talking about the time when your family left the village on the eve of the arrival of the Serb forces, that they went to Hoca river or to Hocanska Reka and that you went there, and that you were told by the Serb forces after the fighting ended in Celine that you could go back to your village.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It is a mistake. Wherever you read that from, that's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But am I right when I say that the KLA members in the village of Celine made third-degree fortifications along the rim of the village facing Bela Crkva, and that on the 25th of March in the morning they offered fierce resistance to the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Whoever knows about that can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that at 10.00 a.m. you left Celine and went away?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I think I told you that I stayed at home in my brother's yard until 3.30, when my brother was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have on the screen a Defence document D002-5628.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, this is your statement of the 23rd of July, 2001, and in this statement in paragraph 4 you say this: "My family and myself went back to Celine three months after I had left, and we went back to our house, the house had been looted, and it was completely empty. I ascertained later on that eight of my family members were killed in the events of the 25th of March, 1999." You never mention that your house had been burnt down.

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Well, if the house has been razed to the ground, what can I say, that it's still standing?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly not, but you had to have known that on the 23rd of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The house was completely destroyed, burnt beyond burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Salihi. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, this completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Now, Ms. D'Ascoli, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, you were asked by my learned colleague early in his cross-examination about the graves of your family members in the yard of your family compound and about the exhumations that were conducted by a team of foreign -- by international team. I have -- some questions. Do you remember which type of graves, where it was in your gardens where your family members were found when you returned to Celine?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. They had been killed there and then they had been buried in a very shallow grave. They had just been covered with soil and that's where we found them when we went back.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Were you there when the bodies of your family members were exhumed by the international team?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: I was present myself, and I gave them the names of the people from my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Therefore, I understand that you were called to identify these bodies; right?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes. There was this foreign team who exhumed the bodies. We were not allowed to do anything to the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I move to something else. My learned colleague also asked you about the people you were with in the forest where you were hiding for two days and also the villages where they -- these people were coming from, where they were fleeing from. Did you have the chance, while you were there, to talk to these people who were with you there in the forest?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, with the people from my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Also with people from other villages?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: No. They, from the other villages, were further away. It was a big surface, about 4 or 5 hectares big, so it was filled with people.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And you were all hiding -- you were all gathered there together, right, so you could see each other and ...

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, the whole population had gathered there and stayed there for three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And how did you know the villages where these other people were coming from?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, as I already told you, they were people who had family in this village and had fled to their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And you were mentioning the Mount Pisjak, and is this mount that you mentioned the area of the woods of the forest where you and your family and these other people were gathered?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, we were there in the woods for three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So is that how you called the area, Mount Pisjak?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salihi, you said you did your military service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Are you then able to distinguish between the uniforms worn by the army and the uniforms worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The police had blue uniforms, as I've already described to you; there were also military forces, but they had different uniforms from that of the police. They had the uniform of the colour of the grass.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Therefore, am I correct when I say that you are able to distinguish between these different type of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell the difference between the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: In answering the questions by my learned colleague, you also mention -- you mentioned having seen different groups of Serb forces there in Celine and they were wearing different uniforms. Do I understand from your evidence that there were forces with both black uniforms and blue uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The truth is that there were all sorts of different groups of them there with different uniforms of different colours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Therefore, did you see both black, blue uniforms, and also other types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The ones I described to you are the ones that I saw, and I could not really look around because we didn't dare. We were surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But in your evidence you mentioned first black and then also some blue uniforms, for example, like in your statement - and this is page 3, paragraph 4 - you described the policemen who arrived to the forest as wearing blue uniforms, blue camouflage-pattern uniforms. Therefore, is that correct that you saw all these different types of -- or colours of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: That's correct. We were under their rule there, they were close to us, and these ones we saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't go farther into that. Did you witness the killing of Agim Ramadani with your eyes?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it with my own eyes because he was very close to where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you see by whom he was killed?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: My last question: My learned colleague also asked you about the place where you went hiding after the killing of your brother and the other members of your family, and this was -- this was a hole where you stayed until the evening before leaving for the forest. Was this place close to the Zeqiri compound, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RESHIT SALIHI
utterances.text: It is close to my brother's compound, not Zeqiri's compound. It is a kind of a hill beyond the houses, our houses and the houses of our neighbours, and that's where this hole was, where I was hiding.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: This is the end of my re-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Salihi, you'll be pleased to know that concludes the questions of you. The Chamber has been very grateful that you were able to come to The Hague again and to assist us with your evidence as you have. You are, of course, now free to return to your normal activities, and the Chamber thanks you for what you have been able to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for inviting me to testify here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The court officer will now show you out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The next witness is ready, Mr. Behar?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, Your Honours. The next witness is Agim Jemini. Before we start with the next witness, I did want to raise a procedural matter, if I could do so at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'd like to make an oral application to add certain new photographs to our exhibit list, and this application relates to photographs that were brought by Mr. Jemini yesterday when he came in for proofing. And Mr. Jemini brought with him a number of photos. As he can explain, they were taken during the time that he'll testify about, and we have checked in our system to confirm that we didn't have those photographs before. And I can just briefly address disclosure and relevance. With respect to disclosure, we did provide advance copies to our learned colleagues last night -- yesterday, in fact. We also, in keeping with our disclosure obligations, in fact disclosed about 42 photographs, although I'm only proposing to make use of about six photographs today. And with respect to relevance, I can just briefly indicate that one of the important elements of Mr. Jemini's evidence is that for about a period of about 30 days he and a number of other men would hide in the fields between Celine and Bela Crkva and at night enter Celine where they found a large number of civilian bodies and buried them. The photographs -- all of the photographs that I'm seeking to tender were taken at that time, during that 30-day period. Four of them show the bodies that were found and in fact some of the people, including Mr. Jemini himself, and two show the men as they were hiding in the fields. In my submission, those will all be of significant assistance to the Chamber if admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Well, inter alia, this morning, today, when we started our work I had a remark that I presented to the Chamber knowing that this would happen, although my learned friend Ms. D'Ascoli obviously cut short the additional information supplied to the Defence so that it was within the limits set by 92 bis. I think that this goes beyond 92 bis, what the Prosecution proposes to do now, and I'm not opposing it because of the time when we received the additional photographs. I have a lot of understanding for it, and I'm sure that I will find myself in the same situation. But if we were in different circumstances, time would not be a problem at all. But here, this has more to do with Rule 92 bis. If we hadn't opposed the admission of those statements without the cross-examination, this would be a finished business; yet now I receive additional information, three pages of it, pertaining to this witness and we received some new photographs, so after ten years. I would just like to note that the basis for the testimony of this witness -- the basic statement is the 17th of July, 1999, and in this statement he mentioned the -- to the investigator, John Zdrilic, that there are some photographs of some graves. So this information is ten years old. It's only about the photographs of the graves. And now we receive a number of photographs that only six or seven might be used that are deemed relevant by the Prosecution. The others, depicting Haradinaj and others including people with rifles, are not of any importance for the Defence, they are not relevant at all for the Defence, and that is why the Defence opposes to the adducing of this additional evidence as the Prosecution has just moved orally. All the more so because the two witnesses were supposed to be heard the last week before the recess, and yet it is today that we get this motion for this evidence to be put in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything in response, Mr. Behar?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honours. Perhaps the one thing I would add is that the reference that my friend makes to the statement, it is true Mr. Jemini indicated that he -- I'll just quote directly: "I also recorded most of the grave-sites with the camera and the film is secured in Celine, and I intend to supply this to the war crimes Tribunal from The Hague." I can indicate first I'm not seeking to tender photos of grave-sites, that's not what was provided to us. However, we did search exhaustively to see if we had been provided these photographs that he brought yesterday, previously, and we concluded that we had not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic mentions some three pages of additional evidence that is proposed. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure, in fairness, what Mr. Djurdjic is referring to. With respect to Mr. Jemini we did provide a supplemental information sheet, but that's largely intended for disclosure purposes. With respect to what the questions I'm intending to ask, I don't anticipate being much over the 30 minutes prescribed, perhaps slightly over in light of the fact we're now tendering these photographs, but I'm not sure what additional evidence is being referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will receive the photographs, six or seven, that you mention, Mr. Behar, assuming them to be relevant to the subject matter when they are offered. If there is some issue affecting the oral evidence that is in addition to the Rule 92 bis statement, some radically different subject matter, that can be separately and specifically raised in the course of the evidence. If the witness could be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please read the affirmation on the card that is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Behar has some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could you please provide your full name and your date of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Agim Jemini. I was born on the 25th of November, 1960.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that you were the mayor of Celine in Rahovec; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you became mayor and how long you held that position for?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: I became a mayor in 1984, and I held that position until two months ago. That would be for about 22 or 23 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us how many people lived in Celine at -- say at the commencement of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: In 1999 there were about 2.000 inhabitants in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jemini, do you recall providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 17th of July, 1999?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I understand that you provided an addendum to that statement on the 3rd of June, 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to read that statement and the addendum before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the information contained in those documents is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that statement and the addendum, that's 65 ter number 02338. I can indicate that they're both together in that package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The statement with the addendum will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00635, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, do you recall testifying at the trial of Slobodan Milosevic on the 7th of June, 2002?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review or listen to the transcript of your testimony in that trial?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender 65 ter number 02353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00636, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jemini, do you recall testifying at the trial of Mr. Milutinovic et al. on the 28th of September, 2006?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review the transcript of your testimony in that trial?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would then seek to tender 65 ter number 05012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00637, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would also seek to tender the exhibits that were associated with Mr. Jemini's testimony; those were all listed in annex B of our rule 92 bis motion. And I can go through those one by one. The first is 01800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's -- sorry, I'm happy to go through each of them. That's an enlarged photo of the destroyed Celine mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I concluded wrongly, but at the beginning of the trial I thought we said that all evidence must be adduced and tendered into evidence and could not be admitted as part of a 92 bis or 92 ter package. utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's partly correct, nearly correct. The Trial Chamber, Mr. Djurdjic, said that the question of the admission would be dealt with at the time the witness came to give evidence. The statement of the witness and the previous testimony having been admitted just now as an exhibit in this trial, that provides an evidentiary basis upon which the Chamber now considers the question of the admission of the exhibit. And in view of the nature of this particular exhibit, it is one which from that evidentiary material, the statement and the previous evidence of the witness, is sufficiently dealt with and described so as to justify admission. Unless there was some particular objection that you made which we would have to consider. Now, that is likely to be the case for many exhibits which were attached to previous statements or which were given as evidence in a previous trial. There will, no doubt, though, be occasions when that is not the case and the Prosecution seeks to tender an exhibit which is not sufficiently dealt with in the statement or the previous transcript, in which event there would need to be some further oral evidence from the witness to provide a foundation upon which the Prosecution's motion to tender the exhibit could be considered and dealt with.
