utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I can now proceed to provide a brief summary of the witness's evidence, and I can indicate that it relates chiefly to paragraphs 72(a) and 77 of the indictment. Mr. Jemini is the former mayor of Celine, in the Rahovec area of Kosovo. He describes the Serb offensive in Celine beginning on the 25th of March, 1999. Serb forces surrounded the village and then shelled and shot at the village. Mr. Jemini hid in the roof cavity of the new house he was building, along with his cousin Isuf. He saw soldiers entering the town from four directions along with police and then looting houses of valuables. He observed the deliberate burning of houses and of the local school. From the house next door, Mr. Jemini overheard the contents of radio conversations involving two men he identified as Serb commanders. The next day Mr. Jemini saw a troop carrier approach the village from the main road, carrying special forces police with beards, shaved heads, and red ribbons. Soon there were 200 to 300 forces in the village, some with white ribbons, some with headbands, they went from house to house. A group of seven or eight men entered Mr. Jemini's house and removed his father, mother, uncle, uncle's son, and uncle's wife. They asked his father for money and later marched everyone outside. They then executed all five of them. Throughout that day, Serb forces looted and burned houses using flame-throwers. Mr. Jemini heard the sounds of automatic weapon fire and screaming. He escaped with his cousin to Zrze, and on the way he saw a large number of corpses near Bela Crkva. Over a period of about 30 days, Mr. Jemini returned to Celine each night, along with others, to retrieve and then bury the dead. In total he helped to 78 victims. He will describe observing police driving trucks along the main roads in Celine and collecting bodies. That is the conclusion of the summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, I am going to have a few very brief questions for you about specific parts of your evidence. To begin with, in your statement and in your previous testimony, after the Serb offensive against Celine began on the 25th of March of 1999, you describe hiding in the roof and making certain observations. And at page 3 of your statement at paragraph 6 you describe overhearing one of the Serb force commanders being told over the radio to stop the offensive on Celine. You describe hearing that commander answer, Yes, we will stop. My question is: After you heard that exchange, did you observe any change in what was happening in Celine?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: At the moment the response was given to the command at 9.00 at night, the offensive was stopped; and the Serb forces took positions around the village, and the offensive was stopped until the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just to be clear, is that something that you observed directly?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because at that time everything stopped. The shooting stopped. We couldn't hear any more shots, and there were no more actions conducted by those forces. We saw that with our own eyes and we could feel it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You described in your statement and in your testimony that the next day, which was the 26th of March, a group of seven or eight men entered your house and removed your father, mother, uncle, your uncle's son, and your uncle's wife. Can you explain to the Court what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: On the 26th of March, when the forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you pause a minute, please, Mr. Jemini. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do beg your pardon. I'm not receiving interpretation of the question. I did not receive any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could ask the question again, please, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Certainly --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. The question was recorded in the transcript, but I did not get a translation into Serbian. So the only thing I need is interpretation into Serbian. My colleague doesn't have to repeat it. I mean, I see it's recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we have the interpretation again. Alternatively, no, we'll go as I suggested. Would you ask the question again, Mr. Behar, then we can get the question and the interpretation so there's no error.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, you described in your statement and in your testimony that the next day, which was the 26th of March, a group of seven or eight men entered your house and removed your father, your mother, your uncle, your uncle's son, and your uncle's wife. Can you explain to this Court what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: At that moment, these persons entered in the basement. They removed my father, my uncle, and the other people from the basement, brought them out into the yard. They asked for money, they asked my father for money; and my father said how much money he had on him. My mother reacted and said, Why are you doing this to us? Then the policemen said to my mother, Don't say anything. Nobody's asking you. At that time, they ordered them to hand over the money, to go to the bedroom and take the money and give it to them. Then they marched them towards the gate of the yard. Outside in the road one of the soldiers shot in the air and the others shot at my family and left them there. This was a tragic moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you say, "shot at your family and left them there," I know that this is difficult, but did any of those family members survive?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'd also just like to clarify. I know that in your answer you've used the terms "police" and also "soldiers." Can you explain who were the men who did this? Were they military? Were they police? Were they other persons?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: No, these were not the soldiers of the 25th. These were paramilitaries, Serb paramilitaries from other units wearing different kinds of clothes with bandannas on their heads and various kinds of weapons on them. They were not part of the regular army. The regular army was there the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You had also mentioned police. Were there also police in that group of seven or eight people that you described?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes, there were policemen with that unit. We call that kind of unit a special unit or Arkan's unit. They were not part of the regular army. They did not have the same uniform as the Serb -- regular Serb army. They had blue or black and blue uniforms. They had bandannas on their heads. Some of them had shaven heads and beards. These were members who conducted the second part of the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. At page 5 of your statement you describe returning to Celine after you had fled. You describe seeing Serb police enter the village each day along with gypsies and burning houses and stealing. And you describe entering the village at night to find people who'd been massacred and to bury them. I'd like to show you some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 5246, 05246.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was taken on the 21st or the 24th when I was in that village during the bombing, I was here. And you can see me in the photograph. I could see the forces expelling the population from Peje and Gjakova. It was about 6.00 or 7.00 in the evening. During the day we could not enter the village because the police and other Roma workers were there, looting the houses. So during the day we stayed away from the village. We just observed the exit and entry points to the village. In the evening we went and saw what had happened to the people who had remained in the village. We saw the bodies of the victims. There are other photographs showing the burial of these people and so on --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a couple more specific questions to clarify. You said the photo was taken on the 21st or the 24th. Which month was that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Not the 21st or the 24th. This was the 21st day after the 24th of March when we took the photograph. As I mentioned in the statement, in 21 days we buried 78 victims. We could not go to the village during the day because we were scared, so we exploited whatever time at night we could to bury the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: My family members who were killed, they were taken to Rahovec. The rest of them, we buried them in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So just so that we're clear, if you're saying 21 days after the 24th, which would put this in the middle of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: There were about 15 or 16 of us in the group. One of us had the task to take the photographs. He was Hamdi Fazliu. He had the task to take photographs of everything we did at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And the bodies that we're seeing there, is that how they were found? Were they gathered there? Can you explain the state of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: The bodies of these people who were expelled were found there at the place they were executed. They were in the same position as we found them. They had been sitting there before the execution and then killed there on the spot. Nobody saw them at the time of execution. We just buried them later. There was the 21st day that we took the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I believe you mentioned that that's you in the background; is that correct? Are you the person who's there walking along the side?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that photo as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00646, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter number 05248.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have finished with the last photograph -- well, thank you, Your Honour. I think that already with the first photograph and the answer, we are going beyond the rules of 92 bis. There was no mention before of such bodies and such pictures and there were no statements made to that effect, by the witness that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's true there was no specific mention. I think you're correct in that. The Chamber's not inclined to see this as part of the Rule 92 bis statement of the witness but as evidence which is being led from the witness, he being here in court primarily so that you may cross-examine. But he being here, opportunity is taken to increase the scope of his evidence. Now, the Chamber is aware that that is a departure from normal procedure, and you're quite correct in that observation. And it is, therefore, a matter which the Chamber will keep under observation. It is not a practice which the Chamber will readily agree to, but given the nature of certain evidence, it would be in the interests of justice the Chamber have that evidence rather than remain ignorant of it. And in those circumstances, the Chamber is prepared to receive such evidence and this appears to be such a case. But the basic concern you raise is one well appreciated by the Chamber and we will keep the matter under observation. And you, of course, if you feel that there is some significant departure that is of great concern to your particular case, should raise the matter specifically as we proceed. Yes, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I -- just to briefly respond to one point that my friend made, I can indicate that this -- the finding of bodies that had been massacred - to use the witness's word - and the burying of 78 people is in his statement at page 5 in the fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think there was any suggestion to the contrary by your learned friend. He was saying this specific evidence, though, is something that was quite beyond the 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, there's a new photograph up on the screen. Can you explain to us -- and I'm not sure, is this a close-up of the same bodies we were seeing before or is this a different -- depicting something else?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: This is a close-up of part of the bodies because of the baby which is characteristic for this photograph. So it's a different photograph depicting a small girl that was executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And do you know who that girl is? Is that someone that you were familiar with?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes, her name is Albana Zeqiri. Her name is on the list of persons that were executed, and I do have documentation pertaining to this execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. But just to be clear, was that a person from your village?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00647, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Briefly, if we could have photo 05251, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this photo and can you tell us what it depicts?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph depicts a burned or charred body of a co-villager of ours. 18 of these 78 bodies were burned, and this can be proven by other original photographs that were taken in the period of time between 24th of March and 15th of April, photographs that were taken on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00648, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can I have up photograph 05252.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, were you involved in the taking of this photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes. I was the leader of this group of 15 or 16 persons that had remained in the area after the starting of the bombing and until the time of these bodies were buried. Together we organised the burial of these bodies. You can see that some persons were placed under the vehicle and then the whole vehicle and the bodies were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that as an exhibit as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00649, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement at page 5 and paragraph 4, you describe how during this time, when these photos were taken, you would hide in the fields between Bela Crkva and Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could we have up photograph 05247, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I can see from this photograph that there's no foliage on the trees. Can you tell us when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: From the 24th of March up until the 15th of May we were in the village. This photograph was taken in spring and this was the area where we took shelter during the days, from the morning until 6.00 p.m. I'm the person standing with another member of the group who is lying on the ground. We stayed in this place during the day hiding and sheltering ourselves because we were scared, and we would remain here in this place until the evening. This happened day after day. We would stay there during the day, and then in the evening we would carry out the burial of the massacred persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me, if you know, how far you would have been here from Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: You mean from Celine?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No, from Kotlina, if you know, if you know where that is and how far that would be from where you were.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: I don't understand it, Kotlina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. Do you know where that village is located?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: It doesn't ring a bell for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that photograph as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00650, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can I have photograph 05253, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: This photograph was taken during the time we were away from the village and had gone to a location where the whole population was gathered after the 25th of March. This is about 1 kilometre in -- from the outskirts of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: From the village of Celine?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how far would this be from the location of the previous photograph, roughly?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: 200 metres more or less. The location of the previous photograph is kind of behind the location depicted on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00651, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Finally could we have Exhibit 00634 on the screen, please. I'm not sure if that's correct. If I could have a moment's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sorry, I see the problem. I actually needed -- it was marked today P00634 from this case. That's my fault. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jemini, do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell what it is?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: It's the village mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us how you're able to recognise it?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: I recognise it because I lived there. There was only one mosque in the village, a sacred place, and that's why I can well recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: In your testimony in the Milutinovic case, you described that this mosque was destroyed in March of 1999. Can you explain to us how you know that?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes. As I said earlier, we moved around the village for two months in the outskirts during the day and in the village itself during the night. Six or seven days after the 24th of March at around 10.00 this mosque was bombed. I think we will look at the photograph that depicts the ruined mosque. At the same day at around 5.00 we visited the mosque. It was completely destroyed. It was just blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, sir, can you explain to us exactly what you saw or heard personally?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: We were about 6 or 700 metres from the mosque. We were sheltering at this distance from the mosque. The detonation was so powerful that could almost equal the detonations of other military forces. And after we heard the sound of the detonation, we saw the minaret falling down, and we realised that the mosque had just been destroyed. Since we were curious, in the afternoon at 5.00 a.m. -- p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we went to see the mosque for ourselves and verify the damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: At that time of that explosion, were there any Serb forces in the town; and if so, who?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes, they were regularly there in the morning. From 3.00 or 4.00 they would enter the village, and that day they were in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you say "they," but who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: These were police forces with other collaborators, people who were looting the village every day. Every day they went into the village they looted the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just have about 30 more seconds and then I know Mr. Stamp would like to briefly address you as well. If I could have Exhibit 01800, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: AGIM JEMINI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the mosque after it was destroyed, after the explosion and after the explosives had been placed there and it was destroyed. This picture was taken on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Oh, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Oh --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had earlier assigned it as P00638.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We must, Mr. Jemini, adjourn for today to continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Your -- we would ask you if you could return tomorrow morning to continue your evidence, and the court officer will show you out now while we attend to a brief procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, briefly I think I should advise the Court that of the three witnesses scheduled for our next week, two of them have indicated that they are not able to come. One, as a matter of fact, is hospitalised and will not be able to come, they are K86 and K79. The circumstances in respect to the third who did indicate a difficulty as well, that is John Crosland, is being confirmed. So at this point in time, Your Honours, I am in the process of trying to find replacement witnesses for then -- for next week Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. And I will -- I do expect to send some communication to all the parties sometime tonight or this afternoon indicating what the confirmed situation is, but I thought I should indicate to the Court the witnesses have quite suddenly, during last night, in fact indicated that they are unable to attend next week. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And reserve witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, last -- next week was a week in which we had three days confirmed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Four days --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Three days --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Friday as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That has -- I've never seen that confirmed in any of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you seen any suggestion we would not sit on the Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, I have not seen a note -- an indication that we would not sit, but we have to go -- in planning the witnesses we have to go by what is indicated as the confirmed dates when the court will sit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the court timetable shows Friday as a sitting day, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No it does not, Your Honour, it indicates that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you may find to the contrary, Mr. Stamp. It says "to be confirmed," but it lists us as sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In any case, the three witnesses that we scheduled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You might say I'm sorry, sir, if that was my mistake before saying "in any case" and going on. Mr. Stamp, there is a lack of attention to the Court's responsibility for ensuring the progress of this trial. Now, we had had a difficulty of this type a little before we broke for the Easter adjournment. We are concerned that witnesses are unable to attend at the last minute. We've asked that you have a reserve witness ready in case that should occur in the future. We will not --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- make more of it at the moment, but please be aware that it is not to our satisfaction the way things are progressing at the present time. Now, you have an immediate and present problem. Two witnesses have at the last minute told you they are unable to attend, and I gather the third one --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- is suggesting a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, that could suggest that they have not had a very adequate notice of their commitment to attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They have, Your Honour. In our submission they have, as a matter of fact, for each of them they were confirmed and a couple of them were subpoenaed some time ago. One is hospitalised, and that is something beyond his control; and I don't really want to go into details about people's personal matters. But in answer to your question, they have been notified in good time. I think I should indicate, since I'm on my feet, that we did calculate for next week that the two to three witnesses that -- or three witnesses that we had on the list would be sufficient to fill the week even if and probably would have to go on into the next week. We thought it would have been very unwise to put in a week where one day would be a holiday a fourth witness, where the three witnesses that were intended to be called for that week were witnesses that we thought would take some time. They are two insider witnesses and one international. So those three witnesses would more than likely have taken the week and that was our main consideration for that week. I would, if I could, do something to ensure that they're here, but I'm afraid, Your Honours, that they have indicated that they can't. And I do apologise to the Court for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will hear from you in the course of tomorrow, no doubt, whether you have made other satisfactory arrangements, Mr. Stamp --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like to indicate to the Court, as I just did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and by the sound of it you are suggesting you hope to obtain substitute witnesses. That, of course, will give rise to a question whether the Defence are in a position to deal with them because there may not be a sufficient time for them to prepare in time. So you'd need to bear that in mind when you're attempting to find further witnesses. And I mention again that there seems not at the moment to be a substitute, spare witness, ready to deal with this sort of emergency. I take it from what you are saying, Mr. Stamp, that it is also the case that you are expecting or have been expecting not to sit on the Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We did not expect to sit on the Friday. We thought that it would have been confirmed sometime before if that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you will for the future understand that if there is a listing you need to be ready for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I indicated, the three witnesses were expected to last for four days or more because of the nature of these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have a discussion over the evening and will indicate the Chamber's position about the Friday of next week tomorrow, Mr. Stamp. We must now adjourn, resume tomorrow at 9.00.
